steps.title: Express and purify Pab1, Hsp40, Hsp104
steps.instruction: Recombinantly express Pab1, Hsp40 (Sis1) and Hsp104 in BL21(DE3) cells and purify them using Ni‑affinity, ion‑exchange and size‑exclusion chromatography.

substeps.instruction: Transform BL21(DE3) with plasmids pJAR006 (Pab1), pEP055 (Hsp104) and pEP057 (Hsp40/Sis1); select on LB agar containing 1× kanamycin (50 µg/mL) and incubate 12–18 h at 37 °C.
Prepare and autoclave 1 L Terrific Broth (TB) for each protein.
Pick a single colony, inoculate 5 mL LB with 50 µg/mL kanamycin, grow overnight at 37 °C.
Inoculate 1 L TB with the overnight culture (1 % v/v), add 50 µg/mL kanamycin, grow at 37 °C, 250 rpm shaking.
When OD₆₀₀ reaches 0.4–0.6, shift incubator to 30 °C; after 30 min induce with 0.2 mM IPTG.
Continue expression 4–6 h at 30 °C, then harvest cells by centrifugation at 3 000 g for 15 min at 4 °C.

Resuspend cell pellet in His‑binding buffer (20 mM HEPES pH 7.3, 150 mM KCl, 2.5 mM MgCl₂, 20 mM imidazole, 10 % glycerol, 1 mM β‑mercaptoethanol) to ≤50 mL and add 1 protease‑inhibitor tablet per 50 mL; freeze pellets at –80 °C if not proceeding immediately.
Lyse cells by sonication (60 % amplitude, 5 s on/5 s off, total pulse time 20 min).
Clarify lysate by centrifugation at 20 000 g for 15 min at 4 °C.

Load supernatant onto a 5 mL HisTrap column (AKTA FPLC) using a 50 mL Superloop; wash with ≥4 column volumes (CV) of His‑binding buffer; elute with His‑elution buffer (His‑binding buffer + 400 mM imidazole).
Pool elution fractions and dilute 2‑fold with Q‑binding buffer (20 mM HEPES pH 7.3, 50 mM KCl, 2.5 mM MgCl₂, 10 % glycerol, 1 mM DTT) to bring salt to ~100 mM.
For Pab1, load onto a Heparin column; for Hsp104 and Hsp40, load onto a HiTrap Q anion‑exchange column. Wash ≥4 CV with the respective binding buffer.
Elute proteins with a 20 mL linear gradient from 0 % to 100 % Q‑elution buffer (Q‑binding buffer + 1 M KCl).
Add TEV protease to Pab1 or SUMO protease Ulp1 to Hsp104/Hsp40 to remove purification tags.
Dialyze the mixture overnight (12–18 h) at 4 °C in 1 L His‑binding buffer using a 10 kDa SnakeSkin dialysis tube.
Day 2: Load dialyzed sample onto a fresh HisTrap column and collect the flow‑through (tag‑free protein).
Concentrate the flow‑through with a spin concentrator and inject onto a size‑exclusion column equilibrated in storage buffer (20 mM HEPES pH 7.3, 150 mM KCl, 2.5 mM MgCl₂, 1 mM DTT).
Pool pure fractions, measure concentration by Bradford assay (BSA standard), aliquot, flash‑freeze in liquid N₂ and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Express and purify Hsp70 (Ssa2)
steps.instruction: Recombinantly express Ssa2 (Hsp70) in BL21(DE3) cells and purify it using a high‑salt Ni‑affinity protocol followed by ATP‑binding incubation, ion‑exchange and dialysis.

substeps.instruction: Transform BL21(DE3) with plasmid pHY024 encoding 6×His‑(SUMO)‑Ssa2; select on LB agar with 50 µg/mL kanamycin, incubate 12–18 h at 37 °C.
Prepare and autoclave 2 L Terrific Broth.
Inoculate 25 mL LB with kanamycin (50 µg/mL) using several colonies; grow at 37 °C, 250 rpm until OD₆₀₀ = 0.4–0.6.
Inoculate each 1 L TB with 10 mL starter culture, add 50 µg/mL kanamycin, grow at 37 °C, 250 rpm.
When OD₆₀₀ reaches 0.4–0.6, shift to 18 °C; after 30 min induce with 0.2 mM IPTG.
Express for 14–18 h at 18 °C, then harvest by centrifugation 15 min at 3 000 g, 4 °C.
Resuspend pellet in Hsp70 His‑binding buffer (50 mM HEPES pH 7.3, 750 mM KCl, 5 mM MgCl₂, 20 mM imidazole, 10 % glycerol, 1 mM BME, 1 mM ATP) with 1 protease‑inhibitor tablet per 50 mL.
Lyse by sonication (60 % amplitude, 5 s on/5 s off, total 20 min).
Clarify lysate at 20 000 g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Bind supernatant to a 5 mL HisTrap column; wash with ≥5 CV of Hsp70 His‑binding buffer.
Equilibrate column with the same buffer containing 20 mM ATP and incubate ≥30 min at 4 °C to saturate Hsp70 with ATP.
Wash again with ≥4 CV of Hsp70 His‑binding buffer.
Elute Hsp70 with Hsp70 His‑elution buffer (His‑binding buffer + 400 mM imidazole).
Dialyze pooled eluate against 1 L Hsp70 binding buffer for ≥2 h at 4 °C (10 kDa cutoff) to lower imidazole.
Add SUMO protease Ulp1 to the dialysis bag and dialyze overnight (12–18 h) at 4 °C in 1 L Hsp70 His‑binding buffer.
Day 2: Load dialyzed sample onto a fresh HisTrap column and collect the flow‑through (tag‑cleaved Hsp70).
Reduce salt to <100 mM by repeated concentration/dilution in Hsp70 Q‑binding buffer (20 mM HEPES pH 7.3, 50 mM KCl, 5 mM MgCl₂, 0.5 mM EDTA, 2 mM DTT, 1 mM ATP).
Load onto a HiTrap Q column and elute with a 50 mL linear gradient from 0 % to 100 % Q‑elution buffer (Q‑binding buffer + 1 M KCl).
Collect all fractions; test each for activity in luciferase reactivation or Pab1‑condensate dispersal assays; pool active fractions.
Buffer‑exchange pooled active Hsp70 into storage buffer (50 mM HEPES pH 7.3, 150 mM KCl, 5 mM MgCl₂, 10 % glycerol, 2 mM DTT, 1 mM ATP).
Concentrate if needed, aliquot, flash‑freeze in liquid N₂ and store at –80 °C. (Note: 280 nm absorbance cannot be used for concentration because of ATP).

steps.title: Prepare Pab1 condensates
steps.instruction: Generate heat‑induced Pab1 condensates, separate them by size‑exclusion chromatography, quantify, and store aliquots.

substeps.instruction: Buffer‑exchange purified Pab1 monomers into aggregation buffer (20 mM HEPES pH 6.8, 150 mM KCl, 2.5 mM MgCl₂, 1 mM DTT) and dilute to 500 µL of 25 µM Pab1 (optionally add 0.25 µM firefly luciferase).
Incubate the 25 µM sample in a 42 °C water bath for 20 min.
Centrifuge at 8 000 g for 3 min at 4 °C (sample remains clear at pH 6.8).
Load the supernatant onto a Superose 6 10/300 size‑exclusion column equilibrated with storage buffer (20 mM HEPES pH 7.3, 150 mM KCl, 2.5 mM MgCl₂, 1 mM DTT).
Collect 0.25 mL fractions; condensates elute in the void volume (MW cutoff ≈ 5 000 kDa).
Determine condensate concentration in each fraction by Bradford assay (BSA standard) and/or SDS‑PAGE with monomer standards (typical 0.5–2 µM).
Aliquot condensate‑containing fractions, flash‑freeze in liquid N₂ and store at –80 °C (avoid repeated freeze‑thaw).

steps.title: Prepare calibration samples
steps.instruction: Create a series of reactions containing defined Pab1 monomer concentrations and a fixed amount of fluorescein‑labeled 19‑mer poly(A) RNA to generate a fluorescence‑anisotropy calibration curve.

substeps.instruction: Keep working stocks of Pab1, ATP (0.1 M), and RNA on ice; keep 1× disaggregation buffer at room temperature.
Prepare a master mix to minimize pipetting error; each calibration reaction volume = 15 µL.
Mix reagents in an Eppendorf tube or directly in a 384‑well plate (see table for exact volumes).
Final concentrations in the calibration wells: 5 mM ATP, 0.2 µM RNA, 1× disaggregation buffer, and the indicated Pab1 concentrations.

steps.title: Set up condensate dispersal reactions
steps.instruction: Combine Pab1 condensates, chaperone mix, ATP, labeled RNA, RNase inhibitor, and ATP‑regeneration system to initiate dispersal; include a blank control.

substeps.instruction: Keep all protein stocks (Pab1 condensates, Hsp104, Ssa2, Sis1), ATP, RNA, SUPERase‑In RNase inhibitor, and the ATP‑regeneration mix (creatine kinase + creatine phosphate) on ice; keep 1× disaggregation buffer at room temperature.

Prepare reaction master mixes (each reaction = 15 µL) according to the table below (volumes are taken directly from the original protocol):

```
Component                | Volume (µL) per 15 µL reaction
---------------------------------------------------
2 µM Pab1 condensate     | 0.67
0.1 M ATP               | 0.10
5 µM RNA                | 0.31
1× disaggregation buffer| 0.75
SUPERase‑In             | 0.66
CK/CP mix               | 0.35
Hsp104/Ssa2/Sis1 mix    | 0.31
```
(Note: the table is reproduced verbatim; use the exact volumes.)
Add the components in the order shown, placing the ATP last to minimize downtime.
Because ~50 % of condensates adsorb to plastic, start each reaction with twice the target condensate concentration (e.g., add 0.4 µM condensates to achieve a final ≈0.2 µM after loss).
Add 15 µL of 1× disaggregation buffer to a separate well as a blank control.
Seal all wells with low‑autofluorescence microplate sealing tape to prevent evaporation.

steps.title: Measure fluorescence anisotropy
steps.instruction: Acquire anisotropy data for calibration and dispersal samples using a plate reader and save the results.

substeps.instruction: Place the sealed 384‑well plate into the fluorescence plate reader set to the anisotropy acquisition parameters described in the Materials and Equipment section.
Run the measurement for all wells (calibration, dispersal reactions, and blank).
When the run finishes, export and save the raw anisotropy data for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Quantify and analyze data
steps.instruction: Convert anisotropy values to Pab1 monomer concentrations using the calibration curve, fit kinetic traces with a logistic model, and optionally normalize to fraction restored.

substeps.instruction: Compute the mean anisotropy for each calibration well and plot mean anisotropy versus known Pab1 monomer concentration.

Fit the calibration data with Equation 1 (modified quadratic binding equation):

y = min + (max‑min)·(RNA+Pab1ⁿ+d) – (RNA+Pab1ⁿ+d)² – 4·(RNA+Pab1ⁿ)²·RNA

where min and max are the minimum and maximum anisotropy values, RNA is the labeled‑RNA concentration, and d and n are fit parameters.

Use the fitted parameters to rearrange Equation 1 into Equation 2 and convert each kinetic anisotropy point (y) to a Pab1 concentration:

Pab1 = (y‑min)²·RNA·(max‑min) – (y‑min)·(RNA+d)·(y‑max)ⁿ

Fit the resulting concentration‑time traces with the logistic function (Equation 3):

y = d + m / (1 + e^{‑a(x‑b)}) – x·c

Extract the maximal dispersal rate using Equation 4:  rate_max = a·m⁴ – c.
Fit the negative‑control trace with a linear model (Equation 5):  y = d – x·c.
Optional: subtract the negative‑control trace from all samples, then normalize the background‑subtracted data to obtain the fraction of Pab1 restored (Figure 7).
Report fitted parameters and maximal rates (e.g., Table 1 in the original manuscript).

description: This protocol describes the specific steps for using fluorescence anisotropy to monitor dispersal of heat-induced Poly(A)-binding protein (Pab1) condensates by the reconstituted yeast disaggregation system (Hsp104, Hsp70, Hsp40). Ssa2 and Sis1 are used as the sole Hsp70 and Hsp40, respectively. We have also used this protocol to test how the presence of additional co-chaperones and/or substrates affects the rate of Pab1 condensate dispersal (Yoo et al., 2022). To prepare the assay, we recombinantly express and purify S. cerevisiae Pab1, Hsp104, Ssa2, and Sis1 from E. coli. We use purified Pab1 monomers to make Pab1 condensates. Fluorescein-labeled 19-mer poly(A) RNA can be ordered from various custom oligonucleotide synthesis service providers including IDT and MilliporeSigma.
